text: Sharp of wit and mighty of arm, Broendulf guards the honour of the Sarls with axe, shield and cutting tongue.
A fine face is no protection against steel, though it makes the resulting scars more memorable.
The sea, the cold and endless war have bred little softness into the Sarls.
I stand where my lord commands, and no enemy shall move me.
When lesser warriors look for courage, they find Broendulf already advancing.
The Jarl's right hand is also his shield. Any blade meant for Viglundr must first find its way past Broendulf.
There is nothing graceful about killing, but Broendulf makes a respectable attempt.
Where the Jarl's authority is questioned, his captain provides an eloquent answer.
The Jarl sleeps soundly because Broendulf and his Huscarls do not.

Pride drove Broendulf to his greatest deeds, and shame taught him his hardest lessons. Both have left their mark.
Look as long as you like. You will remember the face when the axe falls.
Having commanded the most staunch of shieldwalls, Geimdall knows timing is everything when it comes to raising those shields.
Carried in defence of Viglundr's hall, this broad Sarl blade has answered countless challenges to its master's honour.
The mournful blast of Broendulf's war-horn carries far across the battlefield, warning the foe that the sons and daughters of the Sarl are upon them.
The finest Huscarl from the legendary settlement of Oseberg rallies at the thought of timeless battle, hardening his resolve at every blow delt and recieved.
Many have tested Broendulf's guard. Their weapons bear the scars of those encounters; his shield bears considerably fewer.

Upon this blade Broendulf swore himself to Viglundr's service, binding his honour, blood and steel to the fortunes of his Jarl. So long as Broendulf draws breath, the oath endures, and the blade shall answer any who threaten his lord.

Tall and fair-haired even by the standards of his people, Broendulf earned his place amongst Viglundr's household warriors through deeds rather than appearance. The captain of the Jarl's guard must be more than a killer, for upon him rests the safety of his lord, his household and the honour of the hall itself. Broendulf proved equal to that burden. Though capable of meeting the fiercest warrior blade-to-blade, his greatest weapon may be the quick intelligence lurking behind his warrior's temper. His tongue is notoriously sharp, his pride easily stirred and his courage unquestioned. In the sagas of the Sarl, these are qualities from which both heroes and tragedies are fashioned.

A broad shield of ancient Sarl make, Skjaldborg is fashioned from thick northern timber, bound in iron and marked by the blows of countless foes. It has served Broendulf through long years of war, from bloody raids upon foreign shores to the bitter feuds of Norsca. More than once its timbers have been split by axe or shattered by monstrous strength, only for Broendulf to have them bound anew rather than surrender a shield that has never failed him. Among the Sarls, Skjaldborg has become synonymous with the Huscarl himself; when its battered face takes its place in the shieldwall, warriors know that Broendulf intends for that wall to hold.

Raised in the stables of a Jarl's hall and barded in felt, mail and horn, the Huscarl Warhorse gives up a little of the Norscan Warhorse's speed for the protection a sworn champion needs in the press of battle.
Bred on the windswept plains of the north, the warhorses of Norsca are as ill-tempered and hardy as the warriors who ride them.
